I'll think through this as the farmer would, then give the JSON.

**My reasoning (as the farmer):**

I have 10.9 mu. About 3 mu I keep for cotton — that piece is sandy and the wheat does not do well there. The other 7.9 mu I plant wheat in winter and maize in summer, same as everyone in my village.

For wheat, I do what I have done for many years. When I plough in the autumn I put down two bags of compound fertilizer per mu — the 15-15-15 kind, that's about 100 jin a bag, so 200 jin per mu. Then after the spring when the wheat turns green I spread one bag of urea per mu, about 50 jin. My neighbor Old Wang put less one year and his wheat was yellow, so I never cut this. I water four times — once before winter so it doesn't freeze dry, once after greening, once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling. I have the well so I can water. For bugs and rust I spray two times, sometimes three if I see the leaves turning. I use improved seed from the dealer in town, everyone does. I expect about 900 jin per mu — last year I got a bit more.

For maize I plant right after wheat harvest, no ploughing, just push the seed in. I use the hybrid seed, the one with the red bag that the dealer sells — all my neighbors buy the same. I put two bags of compound at sowing and then one bag of urea when the maize is waist-high, at the big trumpet time. I water once or twice if rain is short. Spray for the borer one or two times. I expect 1000 jin per mu, sometimes more.

For cotton I plough deep. I use the pest-resistant seed, the Bt kind — before that came, the worms ate everything. Cotton eats a lot, so I put compound fertilizer and also more potash because the dealer said cotton needs it and my husband agreed. I water two or three times. Cotton needs many sprays — four or five times at least, for aphids and mites and boll worms. I expect 500 jin of seed cotton per mu, if the weather is good.

I do not try new things. What worked last year I do this year.
